newsitem.title: CANADA: Ontario wheat board may drop prices C$10-12/tonne.
newsitem.headline: Ontario wheat board may drop prices C$10-12/tonne.

text.p: Falling world milling wheat prices and a severe fusarium headblight outbreak may lead the Ontario Wheat Producers' Marketing Board to drop wheat prices C$10 to C$12 a tonne when it issues its October projections Wednesday, an OWPMB official said.

"Our pool prices will be going down. It could go down C$10 a tonne, C$12 a tonne," OWPMB secretary manager William McClounie said. "It's on the fusarium and mainly because market prices dropped off in the past month."
The single-desk selling agency originally forecast Ontario's winter wheat output at 1.1 million tonnes.
It revised its estimate of Ontario's main export milling wheat production down to 680,000 tonnes due to a fusarium headblight outbreak.
At least 350,000 tonnes, 51 percent of total production, was expected to grade as feed wheat due to fusarium.
Usually, two-thirds of Ontario's winter wheat crop is exported to the United States or overseas for milling.
The OWPMB's board of directors meet Wednesday to set October pool projections after McClounie and other staff review sales and production prospects, McClounie said.
The OWPMB dropped prices by C$25 a tonne in August.
"This is, for us, a rather important time for price projections because growers right now are just making their planning decisions," McClounie said.
Prices for No1 Canada East White Winter Wheat, in-store terminal or mill, were set at C$210-C$210 a tonne in August.
"Unfortunately, it's been really wet here so we have very little soybeans harvested and this is the time they need to be planting (winter) wheat," he said.
